newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger on tame U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger on tame U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Wednesday as a weaker than expected U.S. producer price index report spurred expectations that U.S. interest rates would not rise next week, dealers said.

"They're stronger now after the PPI numbers. They're actually what moved the market this morning. They were very good numbers," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It's another reason for the Fed to hold (rates steady)."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.10 percent from 3.11 percent at Tuesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened on Wednesday after the Labor Department reported that the producer price index fell 0.6 percent in April, compared with expectations that it would remain unchanged.

The report was seen as reducing the likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at next week's meeting of its Open Market Committee. A U.S. rate hike would likely weaken the Canadian money market and currency.
"It (the data) will probably tend to weigh a little bit more I'd say on the argument for them not needing to move, so the market has rallied," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.46 percent from 3.49 percent on Tuesday.
The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.05 percent from 4.06 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
